title: DoorFlow: Scheduling Robots Through Narrow Doors
hints: LoRR 2026: warehouse-like map
Goal: finish as many orders as possible
en: Good afternoon, everyone. Our project is based on the **League of Robot Runners 2026** competition, or **LoRR** for short. On a warehouse-like map, robots must finish **as many orders as possible**.
zh: 大家下午好。我们的项目基于 **2026 年机器人跑者联赛（LoRR）**。在一张类似仓库的地图上，机器人要完成**尽可能多的订单**。

segs.en: Good afternoon, everyone. Our project is based on the **League of Robot Runners 2026** competition, or **LoRR** for short.
segs.zh: 大家下午好。我们的项目基于 **2026 年机器人跑者联赛（LoRR）**。

segs.en: On a warehouse-like map, robots must finish **as many orders as possible**.
segs.zh: 在一张类似仓库的地图上，机器人要完成**尽可能多的订单**。

title: The task: hundreds of robots, narrow doors
figs: 图 1 背景图
hints: Score = orders finished in 5,000 ticks
3 decisions: assign / route / execute
16 rooms, 31 doors, 1 cell wide, 200–300 robots
Blue path: 8 doors
en: 【指左图】 The background: each grey dot is a robot. Robots pick up and deliver orders for **5,000 ticks**, and the score is the **number of orders finished**. 【指右边 1、2、3】 Every tick, the program decides **which robot takes which order, which way it goes, and whether it moves now**. 【指下方数字】 The official room map has **16 rooms and 31 doors**, most only **one cell wide**, and **200 to 300 robots**. 【指蓝色路线】 This one order passes **eight doors**.
zh: 【指左图】背景是：每个灰点是一台机器人。车在 **5000 拍**里不停取货送货，成绩是**完成的订单数**。【指右边 1、2、3】每一拍，程序决定**哪台车接哪单、走哪条路、现在走不走**。【指下方数字】官方房间图有 **16 个房间、31 道门**，大多只有**一格宽**，车有 **200 到 300 台**。【指蓝色路线】这一单要穿过 **8 道门**。

title: The longer it runs, the slower it gets
figs: 图 2 越跑越慢曲线
hints: Ran starter + 2024 champion
Every curve falls
No errors
We start optimizing from this problem
en: We first ran the official starter program and the 2024 champion's method. 【指三组曲线】 Both get **slower the longer they run**. 【指左边 127 和 37】 With the champion's method, orders per 500 ticks fall from **127 at the start to 37 at the end**, averaged over 60 runs. The program reports **no errors**, so **we decided to start our optimization from this problem**.
zh: 我们先跑了官方起始程序和 2024 届冠军的方法。【指三组曲线】两个都是**跑得越久，越慢**。【指左边 127 和 37】用冠军的方法，60 局平均，每 500 拍完成的单数从**开局 127 降到最后 37**。而且程序**没有报错**，**我们想从这个问题着手去优化**。

segs.en: We first ran the official starter program and the 2024 champion's method. 【指三组曲线】 Both get **slower the longer they run**.
segs.zh: 我们先跑了官方起始程序和 2024 届冠军的方法。【指三组曲线】两个都是**跑得越久，越慢**。

segs.en: 【指左边 127 和 37】 With the champion's method, orders per 500 ticks fall from **127 at the start to 37 at the end**, averaged over 60 runs. The program reports **no errors**, so **we decided to start our optimization from this problem**.
segs.zh: 【指左边 127 和 37】用冠军的方法，60 局平均，每 500 拍完成的单数从**开局 127 降到最后 37**。而且程序**没有报错**，**我们想从这个问题着手去优化**。

title: Robots jam at one narrow door
figs: 图 3 第 3000 拍堵门截图
hints: A week to write a monitoring program: replay tick by tick
Over time, many robots jam at one door (97 at tick 3,000 still heading through door 6)
How did earlier work solve this?
For questions: 38% → 86% of orders left need door 6; 3.4–7.0 vs 26 crossings per 500 ticks
en: To find out what was building up, we spent **a week writing a monitoring program** to watch the replay **tick by tick**. Watching the replays, we found that as time goes on, **many robots jam at one door**. So how did earlier work try to solve this?
zh: 为了找出在累积的是什么，我们**花了一周的时间写了一个监测程序**来**一拍一拍**地看回放。通过观看回放，我们发现随着时间的过去，**很多机器人会堵在一个门上**，那么前人是怎么优化这个问题的呢？

segs.en: To find out what was building up, we spent **a week writing a monitoring program** to watch the replay **tick by tick**.
segs.zh: 为了找出在累积的是什么，我们**花了一周的时间写了一个监测程序**来**一拍一拍**地看回放。

segs.en: Watching the replays, we found that as time goes on, **many robots jam at one door**. So how did earlier work try to solve this?
segs.zh: 通过观看回放，我们发现随着时间的过去，**很多机器人会堵在一个门上**，那么前人是怎么优化这个问题的呢？

title: Prior work: four groups of methods
hints: 4 groups: assignment / route guidance / planners (PIBT: deadlocks & collisions) / jam handling
Each fixes one kind of congestion locally
None avoids congestion at assignment level, whole system
Our question: a global scheduling algorithm?
en: 【依次指四张卡】 Earlier methods fall into four groups. **Order assignment** gives robots close, cheap orders. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread out. **Planners such as PIBT** decide which robot moves first, and avoid **deadlocks and collisions**. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle, or sorts out robots that meet in a narrow passage. 【指底部黄框】 In all the methods we read, each one only fixes **one kind of congestion locally**. None starts from **the whole system** and weighs many factors to **avoid congestion when orders are given out**. So we wanted to try: is there a **global scheduling algorithm** that avoids congestion?
zh: 【依次指四张卡】前人的方法可以分成四类。**派单**给车分近的、便宜的单；**选路**让拥挤的路代价更高，把车分散开；**PIBT 这类规划**决定哪台车先走、避免**死锁碰撞**；**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着，或者处理在窄道里碰上的车。【指底部黄框】在我们读到的所有方法里，每一种都只是**单独在局部优化某种拥塞**，没有一种从**整个系统**出发、同时考虑多个因素**在派单层面去避免拥塞**，所以我们想进行这个尝试，看看有没有一种**全局调度算法**去避免拥塞。

segs.en: 【依次指四张卡】 Earlier methods fall into four groups.
segs.zh: 【依次指四张卡】前人的方法可以分成四类。

segs.en: **Order assignment** gives robots close, cheap orders. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread out. **Planners such as PIBT** decide which robot moves first, and avoid **deadlocks and collisions**. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle, or sorts out robots that meet in a narrow passage.
segs.zh: **派单**给车分近的、便宜的单；**选路**让拥挤的路代价更高，把车分散开；**PIBT 这类规划**决定哪台车先走、避免**死锁碰撞**；**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着，或者处理在窄道里碰上的车。

segs.en: 【指底部黄框】 In all the methods we read, each one only fixes **one kind of congestion locally**. None starts from **the whole system** and weighs many factors to **avoid congestion when orders are given out**. So we wanted to try: is there a **global scheduling algorithm** that avoids congestion?
segs.zh: 【指底部黄框】在我们读到的所有方法里，每一种都只是**单独在局部优化某种拥塞**，没有一种从**整个系统**出发、同时考虑多个因素**在派单层面去避免拥塞**，所以我们想进行这个尝试，看看有没有一种**全局调度算法**去避免拥塞。

title: Everything we tried: mostly small gains
figs: 全部尝试总表（幻灯片上，两个阶段提升不大或变差的版本，按组分六列，关键项标红；数字取自报告第九节）
hints: All versions we tried: early ideas (2 columns) + existing mechanisms tried later (4 columns); key ones red
Matching −1.9%; 4× planning −1%; detours +0.75% (random +1.07%); rerouting +1.18% short tests only
Then: two more weeks writing a congestion monitor → next slide
en: Our own first attempts gave only **small gains**. 【指整张表】 This table lists **all of them**: the first two columns are our early ideas, and the other four are existing mechanisms we tried later. The key ones are in red. 【指第一、二列】 Optimal matching lowered results by **1.9 percent**, and four times more planning time by **1 percent**. Detours around broken robots gained **0.75 percent**, less than a random change. Rerouting by live traffic helped only in short tests. Then we spent **another two weeks** writing a program that **monitors where every jam happens**, to look for a pattern.
zh: 我们自己最早的尝试，提升都**不大**。【指整张表】这张表把它们**全部列了出来**：前两列是最早的想法，后四列是后来试的现有机制，关键的几项标成了红色。【指第一、二列】最优匹配让结果少了 **1.9%**，规划时间加到 4 倍少了 **1%**；绕开故障车多 **0.75%**，还不如随机扰动；按实时路况换路，只在短测试里有用。然后我们又**花了两周的时间写程序**，来**监测所有拥塞发生的位置**，看有没有规律。

segs.en: Our own first attempts gave only **small gains**. 【指整张表】 This table lists **all of them**: the first two columns are our early ideas, and the other four are existing mechanisms we tried later. The key ones are in red.
segs.zh: 我们自己最早的尝试，提升都**不大**。【指整张表】这张表把它们**全部列了出来**：前两列是最早的想法，后四列是后来试的现有机制，关键的几项标成了红色。

segs.en: 【指第一、二列】 Optimal matching lowered results by **1.9 percent**, and four times more planning time by **1 percent**. Detours around broken robots gained **0.75 percent**, less than a random change. Rerouting by live traffic helped only in short tests.
segs.zh: 【指第一、二列】最优匹配让结果少了 **1.9%**，规划时间加到 4 倍少了 **1%**；绕开故障车多 **0.75%**，还不如随机扰动；按实时路况换路，只在短测试里有用。

segs.en: Then we spent **another two weeks** writing a program that **monitors where every jam happens**, to look for a pattern.
segs.zh: 然后我们又**花了两周的时间写程序**，来**监测所有拥塞发生的位置**，看有没有规律。

title: Where jams happen: our congestion monitor
figs: 拥塞监测程序截图（figures/deck/demo/congestion_monitor.html，第 3000 拍；官方房间图 250 台，种子 9700 / 101；三种选路各跑一局，都不控制门）
hints: Monitor marks every jam red; same map, robots, seeds; only the routing changes
Door 6 jammed 91–94% of the run under all three routings; doors 16–18 too
Orders: champion 609, HN-SPF 435, Fortz–Thorup 612 (one run each)
Why? Two weeks of analysis → hand over to Speaker 3

segs.en: 【指截图】 The monitor **marks every jam in red**. The map, the robots and the seeds are the same; **only the routing algorithm changes**.
segs.zh: 【指截图】监测程序会把**每一处拥塞自动标成红色**。地图、车和种子都一样，**只换了选路的算法**。

segs.en: 【指右边柱状条】 We found that **however we changed the routing algorithm**, jams kept happening **at certain places**.
segs.zh: 【指右边柱状条】然后发现，好像**不管如何修改选路的算法**，都无法解决**会在某些地方发生拥塞**的问题。

segs.en: Why? We spent **two weeks** analyzing why these versions did not work.
segs.zh: 为什么呢？我们**花了两周**来做为什么失败的分析。

en: 【指截图】 The monitor **marks every jam in red**. The map, the robots and the seeds are the same; **only the routing algorithm changes**. 【指右边柱状条】 We found that **however we changed the routing algorithm**, jams kept happening **at certain places**. Why? We spent **two weeks** analyzing why these versions did not work.
zh: 【指截图】监测程序会把**每一处拥塞自动标成红色**。地图、车和种子都一样，**只换了选路的算法**。【指右边柱状条】然后发现，好像**不管如何修改选路的算法**，都无法解决**会在某些地方发生拥塞**的问题。为什么呢？我们**花了两周**来做为什么失败的分析。

title: The model, and what makes robots special
figs: 图 4 地图压成网络
hints: To analyze: a model; 16 rooms = nodes, 31 doors = links; door 6 is a cut
Near a door: stand still 4.2× → the problem is at the doors
4 properties: cannot drop; waiting takes a cell; fixed fleet; face to face
So: never drop a robot; decide who goes and when; keep exits clear
en: Thank you. To analyze this, we first built a model. 【指左图】 The **16 rooms are nodes** and the **31 doors are links**; 【指红线门 6】 **door 6 is a cut**: without it, the four lower-left rooms are cut off. 【指黄框】 Near a door, robots stand still **4.2 times** as long as they move, so the problem is **at the doors**. 【指右边四点】 Four properties of robots matter: they **cannot be dropped**, a waiting robot **takes up a cell**, the fleet is **fixed**, and jams come from meeting **face to face**. 【指底部】 So a good algorithm can never drop a robot; it can only decide **who goes and when**, and keep exits clear.
zh: 谢谢。为了分析，我们先建了一个模型。【指左图】**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**；【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：没有它，左下 4 个房间就断开了。【指黄框】在门附近，车停着的时间是走的 **4.2 倍**，所以问题出在**门口**。【指右边四点】车有四个要紧的特点：车**不能丢**；等着的车**占着格子**；车数**固定**；堵车是因为**面对面顶住**。【指底部】所以好的算法不能丢掉车，只能决定**谁走、什么时候走**，并让出口保持畅通。

segs.en: Thank you. To analyze this, we first built a model. 【指左图】 The **16 rooms are nodes** and the **31 doors are links**; 【指红线门 6】 **door 6 is a cut**: without it, the four lower-left rooms are cut off.
segs.zh: 谢谢。为了分析，我们先建了一个模型。【指左图】**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**；【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：没有它，左下 4 个房间就断开了。

segs.en: 【指黄框】 Near a door, robots stand still **4.2 times** as long as they move, so the problem is **at the doors**.
segs.zh: 【指黄框】在门附近，车停着的时间是走的 **4.2 倍**，所以问题出在**门口**。

segs.en: 【指右边四点】 Four properties of robots matter: they **cannot be dropped**, a waiting robot **takes up a cell**, the fleet is **fixed**, and jams come from meeting **face to face**.
segs.zh: 【指右边四点】车有四个要紧的特点：车**不能丢**；等着的车**占着格子**；车数**固定**；堵车是因为**面对面顶住**。

segs.en: 【指底部】 So a good algorithm can never drop a robot; it can only decide **who goes and when**, and keep exits clear.
segs.zh: 【指底部】所以好的算法不能丢掉车，只能决定**谁走、什么时候走**，并让出口保持畅通。

title: Routing or scheduling? The ceiling decides
figs: 图 7 天花板公式
hints: Why did rerouting not help?
26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69, whatever the routes
11 rerouting methods: all worse
So: scheduling → our algorithm DoorFlow
en: So why did changing routes not help? A simple calculation explains it. 【指 1】 The lower-left rooms hold **906 of the 3,614** room cells, which is **25 percent**. 【指 2】 An order needs door 6 when its two ends are on different sides: **2 times 0.25 times 0.75, or 37.6 percent** of orders; the task file gives 38.5. 【指 3 和公式】 Door 6 passes **26 robots** every 500 ticks, so the map can finish at most **26 divided by 0.376, about 69 orders**, whatever routes robots take. 【指底部】 So the real question is scheduling: **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**. This is the idea of our algorithm, **DoorFlow**: regulate the flow through every door, for the whole map.
zh: 那为什么改路线没有用？一个简单的计算就能说明。【指 1】左下房间占 3614 个房间格里的 **906 个**，也就是 906 ÷ 3614 = **25%**。【指 2】一单两头落在门的两侧，就要过门 6：**2 × 0.25 × 0.75 = 37.6%**；任务文件里是 38.5%。【指 3 和公式】门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，所以不管车怎么走，整张图最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69 单**。【指底部】所以真正的问题是调度：**派多少车、哪边先走**。这就是我们的算法 **DoorFlow** 的想法：从全图出发，调控每道门的流量。

segs.en: So why did changing routes not help? A simple calculation explains it.
segs.zh: 那为什么改路线没有用？一个简单的计算就能说明。

segs.en: 【指 1】 The lower-left rooms hold **906 of the 3,614** room cells, which is **25 percent**.
【指 2】 An order needs door 6 when its two ends are on different sides: **2 times 0.25 times 0.75, or 37.6 percent** of orders; the task file gives 38.5.
【指 3 和公式】 Door 6 passes **26 robots** every 500 ticks, so the map can finish at most **26 divided by 0.376, about 69 orders**, whatever routes robots take.
segs.zh: 【指 3 和公式】门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，所以不管车怎么走，整张图最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69 单**。

segs.en: 【指底部】 So the real question is scheduling: **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**. This is the idea of our algorithm, **DoorFlow**: regulate the flow through every door, for the whole map.
segs.zh: 【指底部】所以真正的问题是调度：**派多少车、哪边先走**。这就是我们的算法 **DoorFlow** 的想法：从全图出发，调控每道门的流量。

title: Scheduling 1: a window for each door
figs: 窗口大小原理图（从 Little 定律推出；理论示意，附门 6 的数字）
hints: Our measure: robots on the way to a door (hold an order through it, not crossed yet)
Window (quota) = how many orders may cross a door at once
Little's law: on the way = crossing rate × trip time
Too few: door waits; too many: rate stuck at 26 → extra only queues
Best window = door rate × trip time with no queue (door 6 inward ≈ 15)
Robots: past it, waiting robots block the other side → rate falls

segs.en: How many robots should head for door 6 at once? We came up with a way to **measure how many robots are on the way** to a door: robots that hold an order through it but have not crossed yet. This number is our **window**: it decides **how many orders may cross the door at the same time**.
segs.zh: 同时该有多少车奔向门 6？我们想到一个办法：**衡量在途、会通过某个门口的车有多少**，也就是接了要过这道门的单、还没过门的车。这个数就是我们的**窗口**，用它来决定**同时指派多少个要穿过这道门的任务**。

segs.en: How big should the window be? **Little's law** says robots on the way equal the **crossing rate times the trip time**. 【指左图上半】 With too few, the door **waits**; with too many, the rate stays at **26** per 500 ticks, and the extra robots only 【指左图下半】 **queue**.
segs.zh: 窗口该多大？**Little 定律**说：路上的车数 = **过门速率 × 路程时间**。【指左图上半】车太少，门就**等车**；太多，速率也只有每 500 拍 **26 台**，多出来的车只会【指左图下半】**排队**。

segs.en: 【指橙色虚线】 So the best window is **the door's rate times the trip time with no queue**: about **15 robots** for door 6 inward. 【指右边最后一条】 Going past it is worse than a queue: waiting robots **block the other side**, so the rate **falls**.
segs.zh: 【指橙色虚线】所以最好的窗口是**门的速率 × 不排队时的路程时间**：门 6 往里的方向大约 **15 台**。【指右边最后一条】超过这个点比排队还糟：等着的车会**挡住对面**，速率反而**下降**。

en: How many robots should head for door 6 at once? We came up with a way to **measure how many robots are on the way** to a door: robots that hold an order through it but have not crossed yet. This number is our **window**: it decides **how many orders may cross the door at the same time**. How big should the window be? **Little's law** says robots on the way equal the **crossing rate times the trip time**. 【指左图上半】 With too few, the door **waits**; with too many, the rate stays at **26** per 500 ticks, and the extra robots only 【指左图下半】 **queue**. 【指橙色虚线】 So the best window is **the door's rate times the trip time with no queue**: about **15 robots** for door 6 inward. 【指右边最后一条】 Going past it is worse than a queue: waiting robots **block the other side**, so the rate **falls**.
zh: 同时该有多少车奔向门 6？我们想到一个办法：**衡量在途、会通过某个门口的车有多少**，也就是接了要过这道门的单、还没过门的车。这个数就是我们的**窗口**，用它来决定**同时指派多少个要穿过这道门的任务**。窗口该多大？**Little 定律**说：路上的车数 = **过门速率 × 路程时间**。【指左图上半】车太少，门就**等车**；太多，速率也只有每 500 拍 **26 台**，多出来的车只会【指左图下半】**排队**。【指橙色虚线】所以最好的窗口是**门的速率 × 不排队时的路程时间**：门 6 往里的方向大约 **15 台**。【指右边最后一条】超过这个点比排队还糟：等着的车会**挡住对面**，速率反而**下降**。

title: Scheduling 1: global regulation, like BBR
figs: BBR 控制环与 DoorFlow 对照图（含第 50 轮实测时延比）
hints: Goal: global regulation; a buffer size (quota) per door & direction
Grow until something breaks? robots never lost → no stop signal → queue grows
BBR: max delivery rate × min round trip; min keeps a jam from raising its own limit
Our delay: real time (Little) vs shortest-path time; missed spots 2.2–2.9×
BBR-style cap: big losses gone, small gain +0.08% → fixed quota; watchdog later

segs.en: Our goal is **global regulation**: controlling the crossings at every door at once, with a **buffer size**, the quota, for each door and direction. How should we set these limits?
segs.zh: 我们的目标是**全局调控**：同时控制每一道门的过门车数，每道门、每个方向有一个**缓冲区大小**，也就是名额。这些上限该怎么定？

segs.en: We could let the window grow until something goes wrong, but robots are never lost, so there is **no clear stop signal**, and the queue just grows.
segs.zh: 也可以让窗口一直变大、直到出问题才停；但车永远不会丢，**没有明确的“停”信号**，队只会越排越长。

segs.en: 【指左图第 2 框】 **BBR** measures instead. Bandwidth is the **highest delivery rate** seen, since delivery is never faster than the true limit; delay is the **shortest round-trip time** seen, since a queue only adds delay. 【指右上橙框】 If the limit followed the current delay, a jam would raise its own limit.
segs.zh: 【指左图第 2 框】**BBR** 则是去测：带宽取看到过的**最大送达速率**，因为实际送达不会比真实上限快；时延取看到过的**最短往返时间**，因为排队只会增加时延。【指右上橙框】如果上限跟着当前时延走，堵车就会把自己的上限抬高。

segs.en: 【指下方对照表】 We estimate delay the same way: the **shortest-path time** is the delay with no queue, and the **real time**, from Little's law, includes waiting. 【指右下柱状图】 On spots our first model missed, the real time was **2.2 to 2.9 times** the model: robots were stuck there.
segs.zh: 【指下方对照表】我们用同样的办法估计时延：**最短路时间**是不排队时的时延，用 Little 定律算出的**真实时间**包含了等待。【指右下柱状图】在第一版模型漏掉的窄处，真实时间是模型的 **2.2 到 2.9 倍**：那里有车卡住了。

segs.en: A **BBR-style cap** on those spots removed the big losses, but the overall gain was small, **0.08 percent**, so we kept the fixed quota; stuck robots are handled by a watchdog.
segs.zh: 在这些窄处试的 **BBR 式上限**消除了大的损失，但总体提升不大，只有 **0.08%**，所以保留固定名额；卡住的车交给看门狗处理（后面讲）。

en: Our goal is **global regulation**: controlling the crossings at every door at once, with a **buffer size**, the quota, for each door and direction. How should we set these limits? We could let the window grow until something goes wrong, but robots are never lost, so there is **no clear stop signal**, and the queue just grows. 【指左图第 2 框】 **BBR** measures instead. Bandwidth is the **highest delivery rate** seen, since delivery is never faster than the true limit; delay is the **shortest round-trip time** seen, since a queue only adds delay. 【指右上橙框】 If the limit followed the current delay, a jam would raise its own limit. 【指下方对照表】 We estimate delay the same way: the **shortest-path time** is the delay with no queue, and the **real time**, from Little's law, includes waiting. 【指右下柱状图】 On spots our first model missed, the real time was **2.2 to 2.9 times** the model: robots were stuck there. A **BBR-style cap** on those spots removed the big losses, but the overall gain was small, **0.08 percent**, so we kept the fixed quota; stuck robots are handled by a watchdog.
zh: 我们的目标是**全局调控**：同时控制每一道门的过门车数，每道门、每个方向有一个**缓冲区大小**，也就是名额。这些上限该怎么定？也可以让窗口一直变大、直到出问题才停；但车永远不会丢，**没有明确的“停”信号**，队只会越排越长。【指左图第 2 框】**BBR** 则是去测：带宽取看到过的**最大送达速率**，因为实际送达不会比真实上限快；时延取看到过的**最短往返时间**，因为排队只会增加时延。【指右上橙框】如果上限跟着当前时延走，堵车就会把自己的上限抬高。【指下方对照表】我们用同样的办法估计时延：**最短路时间**是不排队时的时延，用 Little 定律算出的**真实时间**包含了等待。【指右下柱状图】在第一版模型漏掉的窄处，真实时间是模型的 **2.2 到 2.9 倍**：那里有车卡住了。在这些窄处试的 **BBR 式上限**消除了大的损失，但总体提升不大，只有 **0.08%**，所以保留固定名额；卡住的车交给看门狗处理（后面讲）。

title: Scheduling 1: the quota, version by version
figs: 图 9 在途车与过门数
图 8 名额公式
hints: Count: holds a door-6 order, not crossed, even far away; full → order that does not cross
v1 (round 25): one window for all: +0.53% on the champion (small)
v2 (rounds 28–29): per door & direction → +29.1% alone (17 room-map instances)
Size: 8 too tight, 32+ jams → formula 15 in / 10 out (round 41), no worse than hand-tuned (+0.63%)
No control 211 → 3; quota ~25 (knee) → 26

segs.en: The quota counts every robot that **holds an order through door 6 but has not crossed yet**; when it is full, the next robot gets **an order that does not need the door**.
segs.zh: 名额数的是所有**接了过门 6 的单、还没过门**的车；名额满了，下一台车就派**一单不用过门的**。

segs.en: 【指右边第二条】 Our first window counted all robots together and gained only **0.53 percent**. 【指右边第三条】 Counting **per door and per direction** gained **29.1 percent** on its own, on 17 room-map instances.
segs.zh: 【指右边第二条】第一版窗口把所有车一起数，只多了 **0.53%**。【指右边第三条】改成**按门、按方向**数，单独就多了 **29.1%**（17 个房间图实例）。

segs.en: 【指公式】 Hand-tuned sizes were too tight at 8 and jammed at 32 or more, so we derived the size: **2.23 times 247 divided by 500 times 13 is 14.3**, giving **15 in** and **10 out**, as good as the best hand-tuned value.
segs.zh: 【指公式】手调时 8 台太紧，32 台以上又会堵，所以我们用公式推出大小：**2.23 × 247 ÷ 500 × 13 = 14.3**，得到**进 15 台、出 10 台**，和手调的最好值一样好。

segs.en: 【指左图】 With no control, **211** robots head for the door and **3** get through; with the quota, about **25**, at the knee, and **26** get through.
segs.zh: 【指左图】不管门时 **211 台**车奔向门、只过 **3 台**；用名额后大约 25 台，正好在拐点上，能过 **26 台**。

en: The quota counts every robot that **holds an order through door 6 but has not crossed yet**; when it is full, the next robot gets **an order that does not need the door**. 【指右边第二条】 Our first window counted all robots together and gained only **0.53 percent**. 【指右边第三条】 Counting **per door and per direction** gained **29.1 percent** on its own, on 17 room-map instances. 【指公式】 Hand-tuned sizes were too tight at 8 and jammed at 32 or more, so we derived the size: **2.23 times 247 divided by 500 times 13 is 14.3**, giving **15 in** and **10 out**, as good as the best hand-tuned value. 【指左图】 With no control, **211** robots head for the door and **3** get through; with the quota, about **25**, at the knee, and **26** get through.
zh: 名额数的是所有**接了过门 6 的单、还没过门**的车；名额满了，下一台车就派**一单不用过门的**。【指右边第二条】第一版窗口把所有车一起数，只多了 **0.53%**。【指右边第三条】改成**按门、按方向**数，单独就多了 **29.1%**（17 个房间图实例）。【指公式】手调时 8 台太紧，32 台以上又会堵，所以我们用公式推出大小：**2.23 × 247 ÷ 500 × 13 = 14.3**，得到**进 15 台、出 10 台**，和手调的最好值一样好。【指左图】不管门时 **211 台**车奔向门、只过 **3 台**；用名额后大约 25 台，正好在拐点上，能过 **26 台**。

title: Scheduling 2: one direction at a time
figs: 图 10 门口规则示意
hints: 1-cell door: one direction at a time
v1 (round 7): block entering against the flow → no effect (other side still at the exit)
v2 (round 29): other side steps back out of the door area + lowest priority → +27.6% alone (17 room instances)
Round 33: area = 4 cells; 3 cells (rounds 54–57): deadlocked runs 11 → 29 → keep 4

segs.en: Our second rule is the **door rule**: a one-cell door carries **one direction at a time**.
segs.zh: 第二条规则是**门口规则**：一格宽的门**一次只走一个方向**。

segs.en: 【指左下卡片】 Our first version only stopped robots from entering against the flow: **no effect**, because robots on the other side still waited right at the exit, so robots coming out had nowhere to go.
segs.zh: 【指左下卡片】第一版只是不让车逆着方向进门：**没有效果**，因为对面的车还堵在出口，里面出来的车没地方去。

segs.en: 【指上面三格图】 So in version two, robots on the other side **step back out of the door area**, and robots stopped by the rule get the **lowest priority**. 【指中间卡片】 Alone, this gained **27.6 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指上面三格图】所以第二版让对面的车**退出门口区**，被规则拦住的车排到**最低优先级**。【指中间卡片】单独用这一版就多了 **27.6%**。

segs.en: 【指右下卡片】 Later we set the area to **4 cells**; with only **3**, deadlocked runs rose from **11 to 29**.
segs.zh: 【指右下卡片】后来门口区定为 **4 格**；只退 **3 格**时，堵死的局从 **11 局增到 29 局**。

en: Our second rule is the **door rule**: a one-cell door carries **one direction at a time**. 【指左下卡片】 Our first version only stopped robots from entering against the flow: **no effect**, because robots on the other side still waited right at the exit, so robots coming out had nowhere to go. 【指上面三格图】 So in version two, robots on the other side **step back out of the door area**, and robots stopped by the rule get the **lowest priority**. 【指中间卡片】 Alone, this gained **27.6 percent**. 【指右下卡片】 Later we set the area to **4 cells**; with only **3**, deadlocked runs rose from **11 to 29**.
zh: 第二条规则是**门口规则**：一格宽的门**一次只走一个方向**。【指左下卡片】第一版只是不让车逆着方向进门：**没有效果**，因为对面的车还堵在出口，里面出来的车没地方去。【指上面三格图】所以第二版让对面的车**退出门口区**，被规则拦住的车排到**最低优先级**。【指中间卡片】单独用这一版就多了 **27.6%**。【指右下卡片】后来门口区定为 **4 格**；只退 **3 格**时，堵死的局从 **11 局增到 29 局**。

title: Scheduling 2: queue scheduling at the door
figs: 图 11 门利用率公式（演讲专用版：公式和数字相同，只把标题改成不带网络术语）
hints: Door = server with 2 queues, one per direction
Switch 21 ticks; same direction 9 ticks
Every robot: 43%; batch of 10: 88%
v1: at most 80 steps → extra switches → exhaustive service
Theory assumes independent arrivals → tested

segs.en: Looking closer, the door is a **server with two queues**, one per direction. Which queue should it serve, and for how long?
segs.zh: 再往细看，门是一个**有两个队列的服务台**，每个方向一个队列。先服务哪个队列、服务多久？

segs.en: 【指公式】 Switching costs **21 ticks**, while robots in the same direction follow every **9**. 【指 43%】 Switching after every robot keeps the door busy only **43 percent** of the time; 【指 88%】 ten per turn gives **88 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指公式】换方向要 **21 拍**，同方向每 **9 拍**就能跟过一台。【指 43%】每过一台就换，门只有 **43%** 的时间在过车；【指 88%】每次放 10 台是 **88%**。

segs.en: 【指右边第三条】 Our first version capped each turn at **80 steps**, which caused extra switches, so we moved to **exhaustive service**: serve one queue **until it is empty**.
segs.zh: 【指右边第三条】第一版每轮最多放 **80 步**，结果多换了不少次方向，所以改成**穷尽服务**：一个队列**服务到走空**再换。

segs.en: 【指底部】 Theory calls this best when switching is costly, but assumes arrivals do not depend on the scheduler, so we tested it.
segs.zh: 【指底部】理论上换向代价大时这样最好，但前提是车什么时候到和调度无关，所以我们用实验检验。

en: Looking closer, the door is a **server with two queues**, one per direction. Which queue should it serve, and for how long? 【指公式】 Switching costs **21 ticks**, while robots in the same direction follow every **9**. 【指 43%】 Switching after every robot keeps the door busy only **43 percent** of the time; 【指 88%】 ten per turn gives **88 percent**. 【指右边第三条】 Our first version capped each turn at **80 steps**, which caused extra switches, so we moved to **exhaustive service**: serve one queue **until it is empty**. 【指底部】 Theory calls this best when switching is costly, but assumes arrivals do not depend on the scheduler, so we tested it.
zh: 再往细看，门是一个**有两个队列的服务台**，每个方向一个队列。先服务哪个队列、服务多久？【指公式】换方向要 **21 拍**，同方向每 **9 拍**就能跟过一台。【指 43%】每过一台就换，门只有 **43%** 的时间在过车；【指 88%】每次放 10 台是 **88%**。【指右边第三条】第一版每轮最多放 **80 步**，结果多换了不少次方向，所以改成**穷尽服务**：一个队列**服务到走空**再换。【指底部】理论上换向代价大时这样最好，但前提是车什么时候到和调度无关，所以我们用实验检验。

title: Scheduling 3: a bug fix in the executor
figs: 图 12 执行器修复示意
hints: Found by watching replays
Stuck at 22 per 500 ticks
Executor kept robot in old cell's queue
3 lines → back to 26
Hand over to Speaker 4
en: Our third change came from watching replays. Even with both rules, door 6 was **stuck at 22** robots per 500 ticks. 【指上排】 Tick by tick, we found that the official executor **kept a robot in a cell's queue after it left**, so the next robot waited a whole round. 【指下排和 22 → 26】 **Three lines of code** fixed it, and the door went back to **26**. Speaker 4 will now show the whole algorithm.
zh: 第三项改进来自看回放。两条规则都用上了，门 6 还是**卡在每 500 拍 22 台**。【指上排】一拍一拍查下来，发现官方执行器**在车离开一格后，那一格的排队名单里还留着它**，后面的车白等了一整轮。【指下排和 22 → 26】改了 **3 行代码**，门就回到了 **26 台**。下面由讲者 4 讲整个算法。

segs.en: Our third change came from watching replays. Even with both rules, door 6 was **stuck at 22** robots per 500 ticks.
segs.zh: 第三项改进来自看回放。两条规则都用上了，门 6 还是**卡在每 500 拍 22 台**。

segs.en: 【指上排】 Tick by tick, we found that the official executor **kept a robot in a cell's queue after it left**, so the next robot waited a whole round.
segs.zh: 【指上排】一拍一拍查下来，发现官方执行器**在车离开一格后，那一格的排队名单里还留着它**，后面的车白等了一整轮。

segs.en: 【指下排和 22 → 26】 **Three lines of code** fixed it, and the door went back to **26**. Speaker 4 will now show the whole algorithm.
segs.zh: 【指下排和 22 → 26】改了 **3 行代码**，门就回到了 **26 台**。下面由讲者 4 讲整个算法。

title: DoorFlow in pseudocode
figs: DoorFlow 伪代码（幻灯片上；对应报告附录算法 2、3）
hints: Planning round: count per door & direction; give an order only if every door it crosses has room
Every tick: door rule; other side steps back; blocked → lowest priority
Grey lines = 2 safety nets, from the random-door test (later)

segs.en: Thank you. Here is DoorFlow in pseudocode. 【指上半】 Every planning round, we count the robots heading for each door and direction, and give an order only if every door it crosses still has room.
segs.zh: 谢谢。这是 DoorFlow 的伪代码。【指上半】每个规划周期，先数奔向每道门、每个方向的车；只有这单要过的每道门都还有名额，才派这单。

segs.en: 【指下半】 Every tick, the door rule decides which side may move and pushes the other side back; robots blocked by it get the lowest priority. 【指灰色两行】 The grey lines are two safety nets from our random-door test, which I will show soon.
segs.zh: 【指下半】每一拍，门口规则决定哪一边能走、让对面退开，被拦住的车排到最低优先级。【指灰色两行】灰色两行是两个兜底，来自随机门测试，等一下会讲。

en: Thank you. Here is DoorFlow in pseudocode. 【指上半】 Every planning round, we count the robots heading for each door and direction, and give an order only if every door it crosses still has room. 【指下半】 Every tick, the door rule decides which side may move and pushes the other side back; robots blocked by it get the lowest priority. 【指灰色两行】 The grey lines are two safety nets from our random-door test, which I will show soon.
zh: 谢谢。这是 DoorFlow 的伪代码。【指上半】每个规划周期，先数奔向每道门、每个方向的车；只有这单要过的每道门都还有名额，才派这单。【指下半】每一拍，门口规则决定哪一边能走、让对面退开，被拦住的车排到最低优先级。【指灰色两行】灰色两行是两个兜底，来自随机门测试，等一下会讲。

title: The hardest part: does it run as we meant?
figs: 回放演示动图（每处拥堵自动变红；本项目模拟器，种子 9700 / 101）
hints: Pseudocode is short; hardest: real code doing what we meant → most of our time
Rounds 1–8 void: fixed seed + unset variable; 54 runs, only 5 identical
+6.8% from a mechanism that never switched on (picked no door in 32 instances)
Executor bug: only visible tick by tick
Same congestion monitor on our own code: 1,130 vs 609 orders in this run

segs.en: The pseudocode looks short. The hardest part was writing the real code, and then checking that the robots **really did what we meant**. This took most of our time.
segs.zh: 伪代码看起来很短。最难的是写出真正的代码，再检查车是不是**真的按我们的意思在走**。我们大部分时间都花在这里。

segs.en: 【指左边三张卡】 For example, our first eight rounds were void: a fixed planner seed and an unset variable meant the same program, run **54 times**, gave the same result only **5 times**. One version gained **6.8 percent**, but its mechanism **never switched on**.
segs.zh: 【指左边三张卡】比如前 8 轮结果全部作废：规划器种子写死、一个变量没初始化，同一个程序跑 **54 次**只有 **5 次**结果相同。有一版多了 **6.8%**，但它的机制**根本没启动**。

segs.en: 【指右边动图】 We used the same congestion monitor to check our own code: without door control, red spreads around door 6; with DoorFlow, the door keeps flowing, **1,130 orders instead of 609** in this run.
segs.zh: 【指右边动图】我们也用同一个拥塞监测程序检查自己的代码：不管门时，门 6 周围一片红；用 DoorFlow，门一直在流动，这一局 **1130 单对 609 单**。

en: The pseudocode looks short. The hardest part was writing the real code, and then checking that the robots **really did what we meant**. This took most of our time. 【指左边三张卡】 For example, our first eight rounds were void: a fixed planner seed and an unset variable meant the same program, run **54 times**, gave the same result only **5 times**. One version gained **6.8 percent**, but its mechanism **never switched on**. 【指右边动图】 We used the same congestion monitor to check our own code: without door control, red spreads around door 6; with DoorFlow, the door keeps flowing, **1,130 orders instead of 609** in this run.
zh: 伪代码看起来很短。最难的是写出真正的代码，再检查车是不是**真的按我们的意思在走**。我们大部分时间都花在这里。【指左边三张卡】比如前 8 轮结果全部作废：规划器种子写死、一个变量没初始化，同一个程序跑 **54 次**只有 **5 次**结果相同。有一版多了 **6.8%**，但它的机制**根本没启动**。【指右边动图】我们也用同一个拥塞监测程序检查自己的代码：不管门时，门 6 周围一片红；用 DoorFlow，门一直在流动，这一局 **1130 单对 609 单**。

title: Does it only work on this map? Random doors
figs: 换图测试图（8 张随机门房间图 × 2 种车数）
hints: Finally: not tuned to one door? random-door program, 8 new room maps
199 / 249 robots, 640 runs: wins every map, +86.9%
New problem 1: narrow spots → global cap 138; without it −16.9% on one map
New problem 2: rare deadlock 1,114 → 700 → watchdog, relax the rule
Watchdog: no measurable effect on these 8; earlier +2.30% on 15 generated room-map instances

segs.en: Finally, to make sure DoorFlow is not tuned to this one door, we wrote a program that **places doors at random**, built **8 new room maps**, and checked **what else the algorithm needs**.
segs.zh: 最后，为了确认 DoorFlow 不只是针对这一道门的优化，我们写了一个**随机放门**的程序，造了 **8 张新的房间图**，看看算法**还需要什么**。

segs.en: 【指左图第一栏】 On each map we ran **199 and 249 robots**, **640 runs** in total. Compared with the same base, our method **won on every map**, by **86.9 percent** on average.
segs.zh: 【指左图第一栏】每张图跑 **199 台和 249 台**两种车数，一共 **640 局**。和同一底座比，我们的方法**每张图都赢**，平均多 **86.9%**。

segs.en: But the new maps also showed **two problems** that the official map does not have, so we added **two safety nets**.
segs.zh: 不过，新图也暴露了官方图上没有的**两个问题**，所以我们又加了**两个兜底**。

segs.en: 【指左下卡片】 First, narrow spots that the door rule does not cover: a **global cap** from Little's law limits the robots holding orders, **138** on the official map. 【指左图第二栏】 Without it, one new map was **16.9 percent** lower.
segs.zh: 【指左下卡片】第一，门口规则管不到的窄处：按 Little 定律加一个**全图上限**，限制接单的车数，官方图上是 **138 台**。【指左图第二栏】拿掉它，一张新图少了 **16.9%**。

segs.en: 【指右下卡片】 Second, rare **deadlocks**: in one run, two doors one step apart locked each other, and orders fell from **1,114 to 700**. A **watchdog** lets a robot that has waited **300 ticks** at an idle door ignore the rule for one tick; we never remove a robot.
segs.zh: 【指右下卡片】第二，少见的**死锁**：有一局两道只隔一步的门互相锁住，完成数从 **1114 单掉到 700 单**。**看门狗**让在没人进的门口等满 **300 拍**的车，这一拍可以不守门口规则；我们从不拿掉车。

segs.en: 【指左图第三栏】 Deadlocks are rare, so on these maps the watchdog shows no measurable effect; in an earlier test on **15 generated room-map instances**, it added **2.30 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指左图第三栏】死锁很少见，所以在这些图上看门狗测不出作用；在更早一次、**15 个生成房间图实例**的测试里，它多了 **2.30%**。

en: Finally, to make sure DoorFlow is not tuned to this one door, we wrote a program that **places doors at random**, built **8 new room maps**, and checked **what else the algorithm needs**. 【指左图第一栏】 On each map we ran **199 and 249 robots**, **640 runs** in total. Compared with the same base, our method **won on every map**, by **86.9 percent** on average. But the new maps also showed **two problems** that the official map does not have, so we added **two safety nets**. 【指左下卡片】 First, narrow spots that the door rule does not cover: a **global cap** from Little's law limits the robots holding orders, **138** on the official map. 【指左图第二栏】 Without it, one new map was **16.9 percent** lower. 【指右下卡片】 Second, rare **deadlocks**: in one run, two doors one step apart locked each other, and orders fell from **1,114 to 700**. A **watchdog** lets a robot that has waited **300 ticks** at an idle door ignore the rule for one tick; we never remove a robot. 【指左图第三栏】 Deadlocks are rare, so on these maps the watchdog shows no measurable effect; in an earlier test on **15 generated room-map instances**, it added **2.30 percent**.
zh: 最后，为了确认 DoorFlow 不只是针对这一道门的优化，我们写了一个**随机放门**的程序，造了 **8 张新的房间图**，看看算法**还需要什么**。【指左图第一栏】每张图跑 **199 台和 249 台**两种车数，一共 **640 局**。和同一底座比，我们的方法**每张图都赢**，平均多 **86.9%**。不过，新图也暴露了官方图上没有的**两个问题**，所以我们又加了**两个兜底**。【指左下卡片】第一，门口规则管不到的窄处：按 Little 定律加一个**全图上限**，限制接单的车数，官方图上是 **138 台**。【指左图第二栏】拿掉它，一张新图少了 **16.9%**。【指右下卡片】第二，少见的**死锁**：有一局两道只隔一步的门互相锁住，完成数从 **1114 单掉到 700 单**。**看门狗**让在没人进的门口等满 **300 拍**的车，这一拍可以不守门口规则；我们从不拿掉车。【指左图第三栏】死锁很少见，所以在这些图上看门狗测不出作用；在更早一次、**15 个生成房间图实例**的测试里，它多了 **2.30%**。

title: Results on the official room map
figs: 图 14 逐级结果柱状图
hints: 3 fleet sizes × 20 runs
Bars: starter → champion → fixed executor → ours
+140.5% vs starter
+76.5% vs same base (fairest)
en: Here are the results on the **official room map**, with three fleet sizes and **20 runs** each. 【指柱状图，从灰到橙】 Each group of bars adds one step, ending with our control in orange. 【指 +140.5%】 Compared with the starter program, we finish **140.5 percent** more orders. 【指 +76.5%】 In the **fairest comparison**, where only our control differs, we finish **76.5 percent** more. 【指 618 → 1,106】 With 250 robots, each run finishes **1,106 orders instead of 618**.
zh: 这是**官方房间图**上的结果：三种车数，每种 **20 局**。【指柱状图，从灰到橙】每组柱子逐步加一项，最后橙色是加上我们的控制。【指 +140.5%】和起始程序比，我们多完成 **140.5%**。【指 +76.5%】在**最公平的比较**里，只差我们的控制，也多完成 **76.5%**。【指 618 → 1,106】250 台车时，每局**从 618 单变成 1106 单**。

segs.en: Here are the results on the **official room map**, with three fleet sizes and **20 runs** each.
segs.zh: 这是**官方房间图**上的结果：三种车数，每种 **20 局**。

segs.en: 【指 618 → 1,106】 With 250 robots, each run finishes **1,106 orders instead of 618**.

title: Which parts matter?
figs: 图 16 逐项拿掉与加上（演讲专用版：同一组 600 局数据，标签改成不带网络术语的说法）
hints: 600 runs, remove one part
Door rule −25.6, quota −13.6, executor −6.7
Door rule alone +29.7, quota alone +29.3, together +76.4
Quota = how many; door rule = how they pass
en: Which parts matter most? 【指左边红条】 In **600 runs**, we removed one part at a time. Without the **door rule**, we lose **25.6 percent**; without the **quota**, **13.6 percent**; without the **executor fix**, **6.7 percent**. 【指右边蓝条】 Added alone, the door rule gives **29.7 percent** and the quota **29.3 percent**; together they give **76.4 percent**. 【指黄框】 **The quota decides how many robots come, and the door rule decides how they pass**.
zh: 哪些部分最重要？【指左边红条】我们跑了 **600 局**，每次拿掉一项：拿掉**门口规则**少 **25.6%**，拿掉**名额**少 **13.6%**，拿掉**执行器修复**少 **6.7%**。【指右边蓝条】单独加门口规则多 **29.7%**，单独加名额多 **29.3%**，两个一起多 **76.4%**。【指黄框】简单说，**名额管来多少车，门口规则管车怎么过**。

segs.en: Which parts matter most? 【指左边红条】 In **600 runs**, we removed one part at a time. Without the **door rule**, we lose **25.6 percent**; without the **quota**, **13.6 percent**; without the **executor fix**, **6.7 percent**.
segs.zh: 哪些部分最重要？【指左边红条】我们跑了 **600 局**，每次拿掉一项：拿掉**门口规则**少 **25.6%**，拿掉**名额**少 **13.6%**，拿掉**执行器修复**少 **6.7%**。

segs.en: 【指右边蓝条】 Added alone, the door rule gives **29.7 percent** and the quota **29.3 percent**; together they give **76.4 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指右边蓝条】单独加门口规则多 **29.7%**，单独加名额多 **29.3%**，两个一起多 **76.4%**。

segs.en: 【指黄框】 **The quota decides how many robots come, and the door rule decides how they pass**.
segs.zh: 【指黄框】简单说，**名额管来多少车，门口规则管车怎么过**。

title: Lessons: why DoorFlow looks like this
figs: 五条经验卡片（幻灯片上；数字取自报告第九节）
hints: Lessons from all versions on slide 6
Door 6 cannot be bypassed: 14 of 15 rerouting lower → control how many, not where
Cannot drop, take cells → only decide who goes and when
Waiting less ≠ crossing more: credit flow −2.74% → judge by orders finished
Few maps only (7 of 69) → confirm on new maps; measure first (38 of 69 stopped before code)
en: Looking back at all the versions on slide 6, five lessons explain **why DoorFlow ended up this way**. 【指第一张卡】 Door 6 cannot be bypassed: **14 of 15** rerouting methods lowered results, so we control **how many robots go**, not where. 【指第二张卡】 Robots cannot be dropped and take up cells, so methods built on dropping or buffering do not carry over; we only decide **who goes and when**. 【指第三张卡】 Waiting less is not crossing more: **hop-by-hop credit flow** cut waiting but lowered results by **2.74 percent**, so we judge every change by orders finished. 【指第四、五张卡】 Gains on a few maps do not count, so we confirm on new maps; and we **measure the possible gain first**: 38 of 69 ideas stopped there, before any code.
zh: 回头看第 6 页的所有版本，有五条经验解释了 **DoorFlow 为什么是现在这个样子**。【指第一张卡】门 6 绕不开：15 种换路办法里 **14 种**都变差，所以我们管**派多少车**，不管走哪条路。【指第二张卡】车不能丢、还占着格子，所以靠丢包或缓冲的办法用不上；我们只决定**谁走、什么时候走**。【指第三张卡】等得少不等于过得多：**逐跳信用流控**让车等得少了，结果却少了 **2.74%**，所以每项改动都按完成的单数来判断。【指第四、五张卡】只在少数图上有提升不算数，所以要换新图确认；而且**先量能省多少**：69 种里有 38 种量完就停了，没写代码。

segs.en: Looking back at all the versions on slide 6, five lessons explain **why DoorFlow ended up this way**.
segs.zh: 回头看第 6 页的所有版本，有五条经验解释了 **DoorFlow 为什么是现在这个样子**。

segs.en: 【指第一张卡】 Door 6 cannot be bypassed: **14 of 15** rerouting methods lowered results, so we control **how many robots go**, not where. 【指第二张卡】 Robots cannot be dropped and take up cells, so methods built on dropping or buffering do not carry over; we only decide **who goes and when**.
segs.zh: 【指第一张卡】门 6 绕不开：15 种换路办法里 **14 种**都变差，所以我们管**派多少车**，不管走哪条路。【指第二张卡】车不能丢、还占着格子，所以靠丢包或缓冲的办法用不上；我们只决定**谁走、什么时候走**。

segs.en: 【指第三张卡】 Waiting less is not crossing more: **hop-by-hop credit flow** cut waiting but lowered results by **2.74 percent**, so we judge every change by orders finished. 【指第四、五张卡】 Gains on a few maps do not count, so we confirm on new maps; and we **measure the possible gain first**: 38 of 69 ideas stopped there, before any code.
segs.zh: 【指第三张卡】等得少不等于过得多：**逐跳信用流控**让车等得少了，结果却少了 **2.74%**，所以每项改动都按完成的单数来判断。【指第四、五张卡】只在少数图上有提升不算数，所以要换新图确认；而且**先量能省多少**：69 种里有 38 种量完就停了，没写代码。

title: Conclusion
hints: DoorFlow: not smarter robots; how many per door + which side first
Routes no, scheduling yes: +76.5% vs same base (official room map)
Real warehouse: quota per direction + one direction at a time
Simulation only; re-measure for new layouts
Thank you, questions
en: To conclude. 【指 1】 **DoorFlow does not make each robot smarter**; it controls **how many robots head for a door, and which side goes first**. 【指 2】 Changing routes did not help, but **scheduling** did: on the official room map, **76.5 percent** more orders than the same base. 【指 3】 For a real warehouse, this means **a quota for each direction when orders are given out, and one direction at a time in narrow aisles**. 【指 4】 Our limits: all results come **from simulation**, and the numbers must be **measured again for a new layout**. Thank you. We are happy to take your questions.
zh: 总结一下。【指 1】**DoorFlow 没有让每台车更聪明**，而是管住**有多少车奔向一道门、哪边先走**。【指 2】改路线没有用，**调度**有用：在官方房间图上，比同一底座多完成 **76.5%**。【指 3】放到真实仓库里，就是**派单时每个方向设一个名额，窄巷一次只放一个方向**。【指 4】局限是：所有结果都**来自仿真**，换一种布局要**重新测参数**。谢谢大家，欢迎提问。

segs.en: To conclude. 【指 1】 **DoorFlow does not make each robot smarter**; it controls **how many robots head for a door, and which side goes first**.
segs.zh: 总结一下。【指 1】**DoorFlow 没有让每台车更聪明**，而是管住**有多少车奔向一道门、哪边先走**。

segs.en: 【指 2】 Changing routes did not help, but **scheduling** did: on the official room map, **76.5 percent** more orders than the same base.
segs.zh: 【指 2】改路线没有用，**调度**有用：在官方房间图上，比同一底座多完成 **76.5%**。

segs.en: 【指 3】 For a real warehouse, this means **a quota for each direction when orders are given out, and one direction at a time in narrow aisles**.
segs.zh: 【指 3】放到真实仓库里，就是**派单时每个方向设一个名额，窄巷一次只放一个方向**。

segs.en: 【指 4】 Our limits: all results come **from simulation**, and the numbers must be **measured again for a new layout**.
segs.zh: 【指 4】局限是：所有结果都**来自仿真**，换一种布局要**重新测参数**。

segs.en: Thank you. We are happy to take your questions.
segs.zh: 谢谢大家，欢迎提问。
